chunks: Ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Zurarah, who said:

I asked Aba Ja'far عليه السلام about a man who killed another man by mistake during the sacred months. He said: "He is liable for the blood money and the fasting of two consecutive months from the sacred months."
I said: "This includes the Eid and the days of Tashriq." So he said: "He must fast it, for it is a binding right that has become obligatory upon him."

key_terms.أَشْهُرِ ٱلْحُرُمِ: the sacred months in which special legal sanctity applies
key_terms.حَقٌّ لَزِمَهُ: a binding obligation that has become incumbent upon him
key_terms.صَوْمُ شَهْرَيْنِ مُتَتَابِعَيْنِ: fasting two consecutive months as expiation
key_terms.ٱلدِّيَةُ: blood money due for unlawful killing
key_terms.ٱلْعِيدُ: the festival day mentioned as falling within the fasting period

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for expiation when someone accidentally kills a person during the sacred months?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for accidental killing during the sacred months: the killer must pay the diyyah and fast two consecutive months within those sacred months. The Imam عليه السلام further clarifies that this expiatory fasting remains binding even when Eid and the days of Tashriq occur within that period.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5212 - Ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Zurarah, who said:

I asked Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) about a man who accidentally killed another man during the sacred months (Ashhur Al-Hurum).
Imam (as) said: "He must pay the blood money (diyyah) and fast for two consecutive months from the sacred months."

I said: "But this period includes Eid and the days of Tashriq (the days following Eid Al-Adha)."
Imam (as) replied: "He must still fast them, for it is an obligation that has become binding upon him."
